Runs scripts/validate-prompt-scoped-next.ts over many routing scenarios. Two real routing defects it exposed are fixed (journaling vs repair intent, 17a27270f). It now stops at the batch scenario: asking for an exact task id inside an active batch reports task-queue-head-claim-blocked instead of ATM_NEXT_TASK_QUEUE_READY, because the prompt carries no actor and the queue head already holds the batch’s own active claim, so diagnoseClaimReadinessForTasks treats it as a blocker. Whether an actor-less query should warn instead of block is an owner decision; do not relax the gate just to make the test pass.

Root-caused 2026-09-20: taskflow open resolves its output root from the profile path (resolveTaskflowOpenOutputRoot returns the profile repo git root), not from --cwd. The test passes a profile that lives in this repository, so the generated card lands in the framework repo docs/tasks instead of the requested cwd, and the run dirties the worktree. Whether a profile may redirect writes outside --cwd is an owner decision; do not change the resolver to make the test pass.

Root-caused with a debugger: the fixture's "valid active claim" has no lane session, and current policy treats an active claim without a live lane session as repairable (unresolved-claim-lane), not blocking. The gate behaves as designed; the fixture must create a live lane session.
